profile.summary: India's largest paint and home-decor company. Makes and sells decorative paints (interior and exterior emulsions, enamels, wood finishes, putty, waterproofing, adhesives) under Asian Paints, Royale, Apex, Tractor, Ace, Apcolite, SmartCare and other brands; runs kitchens (Sleek), bath fittings (Ess Ess), decorative lighting (White Teak), uPVC windows (Weatherseal) and furnishings (Nilaya); industrial coatings through two 50:50 JVs with PPG of the US; paint operations in 13 countries outside India.

callPoints: Volume growth ~9% 'across the months'; rural and T3/T4 towns ahead of T1/T2 cities; B2B projects strong in urban markets.

Weighted price increase ~7% in Q1 (taken in April, May and June); with the mix of increases, the pricing effect should be ~8-9% in Q2. No further increase intended 'unless the situation really becomes alarming'.
Material inflation ~25% in Q1; low-cost finished-goods inventory 'seeped through in 1Q'; Q2 is seasonally lower-margin and will carry the higher-cost inventory.
FY27 guidance kept: decorative volume growth 8-10%; consolidated PBDIT margin 18-20%.
Value growth will stay above volume growth 'till the time we get into pricing corrections'; price changes in H2 'could trigger demand even further' (i.e. cuts are possible if raw materials fall).

Competitive intensity 'seems to be at an all-time high'; discounting most intense in economy products, where contractors can be converted with higher discounts. Medium and large players gained from smaller ones during supply disruptions.

VAM-VAE plant (Dahej): first phase from August 2026; 1,00,000 t VAM and 1,50,000 t VAE; 2-2.5 years to approach 150,000 t; 300-500 bp gross-margin benefit on products that use in-house emulsion. White cement plant in Fujairah (UAE) 'fully operational'.
Industrial JV price increases lag (key accounts); margins down ~120 bp in both JVs; management expects industrial to keep outgrowing decorative.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Asian Paints (consolidated, Rs crore). Asian Paints reports no operating segments, so revenue and EBITDA are built on two lines that reconcile exactly to reported figures: STANDALONE (Asian Paints Ltd: decorative paints in India, ~97% of it, plus kitchens and bath fittings) and SUBSIDIARIES & CONSOLIDATION (consolidated less standalone: international, Asian Paints PPG industrial coatings, White Teak, Weatherseal, white cement, less eliminations). History in research/segments.json. EBITDA = operating profit before other income. History is attributable to Asian Paints' shareholders (Screener Net Profit replaced by Profit for EPS, see tools/authoring/ASIANPAINT.patch.js); the tax line also carries minorities. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

segments.name: Standalone (decorative India, kitchens, bath)
segments._why: FY27 +14%: Q1 standalone revenue +16.7% (decorative volume +9.0%, value +16.6% with ~7% weighted price and a better mix). Price increases of ~13-14% at list level were in place by June, so Q2-Q3 carry ~8-9% price on volume growth near the 8-10% guidance; but management has flagged possible price cuts in H2 if crude-linked inputs keep easing, Q3-Q4 face a higher base (Q4FY26 +10%), and the economy range (putty, low-end emulsions) keeps growing faster than premium. We assume volume ~9% and price/mix ~5% for the year (Q2 ~+15%, H2 ~+11%). FY28 +8%: price laps and partly reverses; volume ~8-9% with the long-run value-volume gap of 3-4% narrowing to ~1% as premium grows. FY29 +8%: volume ~8-9%, small negative mix. Brokers model consolidated revenue +14-17% in FY27 and +6-11% in FY28.
segments._marginWhy: Standalone EBITDA margin (Screener basis, before other income) was 24.3% (FY21), 18.2% (FY22, raw-material spike), 22.6% (FY24, deflation), 18.8% (FY25, price cuts and competition) and 20.1% (FY26); Q1FY27 21.9% on low-cost inventory. Q2FY27 carries ~25% material inflation against ~8-9% price (PL models ~70 bp YoY gross-margin contraction in Q2); H2 depends on crude. FY27 20.3%; FY28-29 20.6% as VAM-VAE (300-500 bp gross-margin benefit on products using in-house VAE, 2-2.5 year ramp) offsets continued discounting by Birla Opus and JSW. Consolidated margin ~19.0-19.2%, inside management's 18-20% band and in line with brokers (19.0-19.4%). We do not return to FY24's 22.6%: competition has changed the industry's pricing.

segments.name: Subsidiaries & consolidation (international, industrial, decor)
segments._why: Consolidated less standalone revenue grew 10.6% in FY26 (Rs4,815 cr) and 26.9% in Q1FY27 (Rs1,359 cr): international +27% (+20% constant currency; FY26 Rs3,340 cr), Asian Paints PPG +21% (FY26 Rs1,334 cr), Weatherseal +11%, White Teak -7%. FY27 +16% (international ~+15% with Middle East conflict risk and Ethiopia currency, APPPG ~+17%, white cement ramp-up); FY28-29 +11% (international high single digit to low double digit, industrial ~15%).
segments._marginWhy: Consolidated less standalone EBITDA margin: 10.0% (FY20), 5.5% (FY22), 12.7% (FY24), 10.3% (FY25), 10.7% (FY26), 11.6% (Q1FY27). International PBT margin rose to 8.5% (Q4FY26) and 7.9% (Q1FY27) after exiting Indonesia; APPPG PBT margin 6.9-8% (price increases lag); White Teak, Weatherseal and white cement still lose money (FY26 net losses Rs56 cr, Rs23 cr, Rs43 cr). 11% a year: international gains offset by start-up losses.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated (none: the two lines sum to reported EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Standalone plus subsidiaries-and-consolidation equals reported consolidated revenue and EBITDA by construction (history in segments.json).
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash-flow capex Rs2,496 cr (FY24), Rs1,830 cr (FY25), Rs1,487 cr (FY26; standalone Rs1,178 cr). Committed: balance of the ~Rs3,250 cr VAM-VAE project (Dahej, first phase from Aug-2026), a second UAE paint plant (~Rs340 cr), a 4 lakh KL Madhya Pradesh paint plant (~Rs2,000 cr, within three years of environmental clearance), plus ~Rs500-600 cr of maintenance, stores and IT. Rs1,400 cr a year (3.4% of FY27E revenue falling to 3.0%).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs1,229 cr = 8.4% of average gross block (Rs14,707 cr); Q1FY27 Rs304 cr (Rs1,216 cr annualised). The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs1,849 cr at Mar-26) and depreciates capex at once; VAM-VAE capitalisation from FY27 adds depreciation. 8.2% gives Rs1,312 cr in FY27E.

otherTreasury._why: Term deposits with more than 12 months' maturity sit in other financial assets (non-current Rs1,153 cr + current Rs1,285 cr at Mar-26, AR FY26 consolidated note 8), i.e. inside Screener's 'other assets'. They are treasury, not working capital.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to cash, investments and term deposits less borrowings (incl. leases): Rs6,646 cr at Mar-26 (cash Rs1,074 cr + investments Rs7,062 cr + deposits Rs2,439 cr - borrowings Rs3,929 cr). FY26 treasury income (interest Rs181 cr + FVTPL gains Rs287 cr + dividends Rs2 cr = Rs470 cr) was ~5.5% of average gross treasury but ~8.5% of average net cash, because borrowing costs are shown separately as interest. 7.5% on net cash.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: share of profit of the PPG Asian Paints associate (Rs141 cr FY25, Rs166 cr FY26; PPGAP revenue +13.5% in Q1FY27) and other non-operating income ('others' Rs237 cr, royalty, insurance claims ~Rs250 cr in FY26). Rs420 / 450 / 480 cr. FY26 Screener other income (Rs728 cr) was after Rs158 cr of exceptional charges; Q1FY27 Rs279 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs195 cr; Q1FY27 Rs48 cr. Borrowings Rs3,929 cr at Mar-26 incl. Rs1,636 cr leases and Rs805 cr long-term debt taken over with the polymers subsidiary (VAM-VAE).
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: there is no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT Rs2,096 cr, attributable PAT Rs1,539 cr = 26.6% (tax ~25.6% + minorities ~1.0%). FY26: tax Rs1,609 cr on PBT Rs6,003 cr (26.8%, incl. non-deductible exceptional items) and minorities Rs76 cr. Minorities are mainly PPG's 50% of Asian Paints PPG and partners in Nepal, Egypt, Ethiopia, Weatherseal and the UAE white-cement unit.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend policy: 60% of standalone PAT before exceptional items (FY25 and FY26: Rs24.80 and Rs27.50 a share). 60% of consolidated EPS is close to that.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, defensive consumer franchise; below-market sensitivity (Ke 11.3%).
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; paint demand tracks housing, repainting and penetration. The house range is 5-6%; we use 6% for the category leader, as for Pidilite.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~8% to 8% over 15 years: per-capita paint use in India is low, so volume can compound at high single digits for long, but competition caps price and mix.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin ~19.2% in FY29E held near 19%, the middle of management's 18-20% band: the new competitive structure does not allow a return to the 21-22% of FY21/FY24.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~3% of revenue to 3% (maintenance plus regular capacity additions).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Birla Opus and JSW shift from share-chasing to profitability (Nomura's thesis), discounting eases, price increases largely stick as inputs fall, and VAM-VAE delivers its 300-500 bp benefit on a growing share of products; decorative volume 10-11%, standalone margin ~21.5%, consolidated ~20%, the top of the band.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Inflation persists into H2 while competitors keep discounting; Asian Paints cuts prices or raises rebates to defend share, Birla Opus keeps gaining ~30 bp a quarter and JSW Dulux turns aggressive; decorative value growth falls to low single digits in FY28 and consolidated margin slips to ~17.5%, below the 18-20% band (as in FY22 and FY25).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Asian Paints: every broker that discloses a method uses P/E on FY28E EPS (Motilal Oswal, ICICI Securities and Anand Rathi 50x, MNCL 52x, Prabhudas Lilladher ~46.5x; Jul-2026). 43x = the stock's 59.6x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (forwardMedian; no trough years) cut by the ~28% median de-rating of six paint and consumer peers versus their five-year median P/E at 30-Sep-2026 (Berger -27%, Kansai -44%, Indigo -25%, Pidilite -35%, HUL -27%, Astral -29%) = 42.9x. No further growth adjustment: our FY26-29E EPS growth (~14% a year, ~10% after FY27's price boost) is above the 7% of FY21-26, and the competition risk sits in our margin forecast (19%, not 21-22%). 43x is close to the 44x median of the last two years. Bull 48x (its 25th-percentile forward P/E since 2021); bear 38x (~5% below its lowest forward P/E since 2016, 40x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 24x Sep-28E EBITDA = Asian Paints' 39.9x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, less the same ~28% sector de-rating (28.7x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~22% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (Rs7,240 cr).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.

cover.headline: Volumes are back, pricing power is not: a great franchise in a permanently tougher market, now priced about right
cover.lead: Asian Paints is India's largest paint company, with ~1.7 lakh retail touchpoints and 27 plants. Since Grasim launched Birla Opus in Feb-2024 (now the #3 player, Q1FY27 paint revenue ₹1,661 cr, +64%) and JSW bought Akzo Nobel India, it has lost share (59% to 52% of branded decorative paints in the year to Mar-2025, Elara) and pricing power: value growth trailed volume by 4-7 points for two years. Volumes recovered to +8.7% in FY26 and +9.0% in Q1FY27, and price rises to offset the 2026 input spike lifted Q1FY27 revenue 18% and EBITDA 34%, helped by low-cost inventory that management says has now run out. The street values Asian Paints on **P/E (46.5-52x FY28E EPS)**. We forecast EPS of ₹54.6 in FY27E and ₹60.6 in FY28E, in line with the street. Applying **43x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹63.6** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,330, DCF ₹1,386. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Decorative volume growth recovered from −0.5% (Q2FY25) to 10.9%, 7.9%, 12.4% and 9.0% in the last four quarters; FY27 guidance is 8-10%. In the 2026 supply shock large players gained from small ones. Industrial JVs and international (+27% in Q1FY27) add growth.

arguments.h: Pricing power has been lost, for now
arguments.p: FY26 value growth was only 4.3% on 8.7% volume: price cuts, rebates and down-trading. Discounting has seen "no let-up" (MD, May-2026) and competition is "at an all-time high" (Jul-2026). Birla Opus gained another ~30 bp of share in Q1FY27 alone. Q1FY27's value growth (+16.6%) is price pass-through, not regained pricing power.

arguments.h: Margins: inside the band, not back to FY24
arguments.p: Consolidated EBITDA margin: 21.4% (FY24), 17.7% (FY25), 18.8% (FY26), 20.6% in Q1FY27 on cheap inventory; ~25% input inflation hits Q2. We model {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}, inside the 18-20% guidance. VAM-VAE (from Aug-2026) helps from FY28.

At ₹2,403 the stock trades at 44.0x our FY27E and 39.6x FY28E EPS, against a 59.6x median forward P/E since 2021. After the sector's ~28% de-rating our 43x gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, just short of a BUY. A DCF at an 11.3% cost of equity gives only ₹1,386: the price still assumes decades of growth.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): how much margin the high-cost inventory takes, and whether volumes hold in the 8-10% band through the festive season.

sections.title: A growing market that turned from a cosy oligopoly into a price war

blocks.p: India's decorative paint market grows with new homes, repainting and the shift from lime wash and unorganised brands to branded emulsions. For decades it was a stable oligopoly: Asian Paints, Berger, Kansai Nerolac and Akzo Nobel (Dulux) together held most of the branded market, raised prices together and earned high returns. That changed in 2024. Grasim launched Birla Opus with ~₹10,000 cr of planned investment (Grasim) and a large capacity build-out, and in 2025 JSW Paints bought control of Akzo Nobel India (now JSW Dulux). New entrants pay dealers more, give contractors bigger schemes and discount the economy range hardest.

The cost side is a petrochemical cycle with one big exception: titanium dioxide (TiO2), the white pigment, is the largest single input and is not linked to crude. Monomers, solvents and emulsions are. The West Asia conflict from early 2026 pushed material costs up ~20-25%; the industry raised prices ~13-14% in steps between March and June. Material is only ~35-40% of what a household pays per square foot (labour is the rest), which is why demand has absorbed price rises so far.

bullets: **Where the fight is.** Management says discounting is most intense in the economy range (putty, low-end emulsions), where "you can really convert a contractor much better if you were to do higher discounting". Asian Paints has chosen to defend volume there, which is why its mix was negative for two years.

**What has gone right.** Volume growth is back to 8-12%; in the 2026 supply shock medium and large players took share from small ones; premium and luxury ranges and new products (17% of revenue) are growing; B2B projects and industrial coatings are strong.

**What the bulls say.** Nomura upgraded in May-2026 arguing Birla Opus is shifting from chasing share to profitability and the price war may have peaked; Elara thinks significant share loss "may be in the past". Grasim's Q1FY27 commentary still talks of "sustaining market share gains".

**Regulation.** The CCI ordered a DG investigation on 1-Jul-2025 into Grasim's complaint that Asian Paints hindered Birla Opus's entry by pressuring dealers, suppliers and landlords. The company says it has a reasonable defence; the outcome is open.

blocks.callout: **Our verdict:** the share loss is slowing but has not reversed, and pricing power has not come back: Q1FY27's strong value growth is cost pass-through that may partly reverse in H2 if inputs fall. We think margins have reset from the 21-22% of FY21 and FY24 to the 18-20% band for good, and we model 19.0-19.2%. Our 43x target multiple prices a still-dominant but no-longer-unchallenged leader; the street's 50x is closer to the pre-2024 multiple.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Asian Paints still has the strongest brand, the deepest dealer and tinting network, the lowest cost to serve and, from FY27, a backward-integration edge nobody else in India has. But the last two years proved that its biggest moat, the dealer network, can be copied by a rival willing to spend: Birla Opus built a national network and reached #3 in about two years by paying dealers and contractors more. The moat now protects **volume and leadership**, not **price**. A franchise that once set prices for the industry now has to match competitors' discounts. That is a narrower moat than the one the 60x-80x multiples of 2021-24 were paying for.

blocks.p: Asian Paints' revenue grew from ₹14,271 cr in FY16 to ₹35,584 cr in FY26, about 9.6% a year, and profit attributable to shareholders from ₹1,745 cr to ₹4,325 cr, about 9.5% a year. The last five years were rough. Revenue jumped 34% in FY22 and 19% in FY23 as the company passed on a raw-material spike, then stalled: +3% in FY24, −4.5% in FY25 (price cuts, weak demand and Birla Opus's launch) and +5% in FY26. EPS went from ₹32.7 (FY21) to ₹56.9 (FY24) and back to ₹38.2 (FY25) and ₹45.1 (FY26): only 6.6% a year over FY21-26.

blocks.p: Asian Paints used to be one of India's highest-return companies: ROCE of 42% in FY15-16 and 29-38% in FY19-FY24. It was 26% in FY25 and FY26. Two reasons. Margins fell (above). And the company stepped up investment: capex was ₹5,813 cr in FY24-26 against ₹2,286 cr in FY21-23, for new paint capacity, the VAM-VAE emulsion plant at Dahej (~₹3,250 cr committed), a white-cement plant in the UAE and home-decor businesses (White Teak, Weatherseal) that still lose money. Operating cash flow was ₹17,616 cr over FY24-26 (FY26 ₹7,088 cr, helped by a ₹976 cr inventory release) and dividends ₹8,116 cr.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts, strong cash, recurring "one-off" impairments

bullets: **Cash backs profit.** Operating cash flow was 164% of attributable profit in FY26 (helped by a ₹976 cr inventory release), 121% in FY25 and 112% in FY24; over FY15-26 cash from operations (₹39,057 cr) exceeded profit (₹35,707 cr). FY22 (33%) was the exception, when inventory was built during the input spike.

**"Exceptional" items keep recurring.** −₹363 cr in FY25 (Ethiopia devaluation, White Teak and Causeway impairments, Indonesia exit) and −₹158 cr in FY26 (White Teak intangibles ₹94 cr, new labour code ₹64 cr). Most of it is the cost of home-decor acquisitions that did not work. We treat them as real costs of capital allocation, not as noise.

**Other income is meaningful.** ₹728 cr in FY26 on Screener's basis (after exceptional items), 12% of pre-tax profit. It includes ₹287 cr of mark-to-market gains on funds, ₹181 cr of interest and ₹166 cr share of PPG Asian Paints' profit.

**Minorities.** Screener's consolidated "Net Profit" is before minorities (₹4,395 cr in FY26) while EPS is after (₹4,325 cr); we use the attributable figure throughout. Minorities (₹42-97 cr a year) are mainly PPG's half of Asian Paints PPG.

**Revenue recognition.** Revenue is net of discounts and schemes; the auditor's key audit matter for the parent is revenue cut-off, the second is goodwill impairment (₹219 cr). Rising dealer schemes reduce reported revenue rather than appear as costs, which is why value growth trailed volume.

**Disclosure.** No segment reporting; decorative revenue and margins are not disclosed. Volume growth is disclosed only as a percentage. Business-line PBT is given for the JVs, international and home decor.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit (Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP; S R B C & Co proposed from the 2026 AGM under mandatory rotation), strong cash conversion and a simple balance sheet. The things to watch are the size of dealer schemes netted from revenue, and further impairments in home decor.

sections.title: Net cash of ~₹6,600 cr; working capital tightened in FY26

blocks.p: Asian Paints is net cash. At Mar-2026 it held ₹1,074 cr of cash, ₹7,062 cr of investments and ₹2,439 cr of term deposits (inside other financial assets), against ₹3,929 cr of borrowings, of which ₹1,636 cr are leases and ₹805 cr long-term debt taken over with the polymers subsidiary that is building VAM-VAE. Net cash was ~₹6,600 cr. Working-capital days fell from 52 to 38 in FY26 as inventory came down from 142 to 118 days; receivables have stayed at ~46 days, above the 30-38 days of FY15-20, a sign of more generous dealer credit in a competitive market.

sections.title: The street: mostly Buy, targets ₹2,720-3,750, set when the stock was ~₹2,760

blocks.p: Ten houses published around the Q1FY27 results (28-31 Jul 2026). Buys: ICICI Securities ₹3,180, Anand Rathi ₹3,180 (upgraded), Axis Securities ₹3,270, MNCL ₹3,165 (initiation) and Nomura ₹3,750 (upgraded to Buy in May). Accumulate: Elara ₹3,100 and Deven Choksey ₹2,970. Neutral/Hold: Motilal Oswal ₹3,050 and Prabhudas Lilladher ₹2,720. JM Financial raised its target to ₹2,930. The median target is ~₹3,165 (average ₹3,149), set when the stock was ~₹2,720-2,760; by 30-Sep-2026 the price had fallen to ₹2,403 with the rest of the paint and consumer sector, so the same targets now imply ~32% upside. Every house that discloses a method uses **P/E on FY28E EPS, at 46.5-52x**. Before the results, a consensus of 35 analysts had an average target of ₹2,848. Bulls focus on volume recovery, backward integration and an end to the price war; bears and neutrals on competition, input costs and valuation.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Asian Paints (consolidated, Rs crore). Asian Paints reports no operating segments, so revenue and EBITDA are built on two lines that reconcile exactly to reported figures: STANDALONE (Asian Paints Ltd: decorative paints in India, ~97% of it, plus kitchens and bath fittings) and SUBSIDIARIES & CONSOLIDATION (consolidated less standalone: international, Asian Paints PPG industrial coatings, White Teak, Weatherseal, white cement, less eliminations). History in research/segments.json. EBITDA = operating profit before other income. History is attributable to Asian Paints' shareholders (Screener Net Profit replaced by Profit for EPS, see tools/authoring/ASIANPAINT.patch.js); the tax line also carries minorities. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

segments.name: Standalone (decorative India, kitchens, bath)
segments._why: FY27 +14%: Q1 standalone revenue +16.7% (decorative volume +9.0%, value +16.6% with ~7% weighted price and a better mix). Price increases of ~13-14% at list level were in place by June, so Q2-Q3 carry ~8-9% price on volume growth near the 8-10% guidance; but management has flagged possible price cuts in H2 if crude-linked inputs keep easing, Q3-Q4 face a higher base (Q4FY26 +10%), and the economy range (putty, low-end emulsions) keeps growing faster than premium. We assume volume ~9% and price/mix ~5% for the year (Q2 ~+15%, H2 ~+11%). FY28 +8%: price laps and partly reverses; volume ~8-9% with the long-run value-volume gap of 3-4% narrowing to ~1% as premium grows. FY29 +8%: volume ~8-9%, small negative mix. Brokers model consolidated revenue +14-17% in FY27 and +6-11% in FY28.
segments._marginWhy: Standalone EBITDA margin (Screener basis, before other income) was 24.3% (FY21), 18.2% (FY22, raw-material spike), 22.6% (FY24, deflation), 18.8% (FY25, price cuts and competition) and 20.1% (FY26); Q1FY27 21.9% on low-cost inventory. Q2FY27 carries ~25% material inflation against ~8-9% price (PL models ~70 bp YoY gross-margin contraction in Q2); H2 depends on crude. FY27 20.3%; FY28-29 20.6% as VAM-VAE (300-500 bp gross-margin benefit on products using in-house VAE, 2-2.5 year ramp) offsets continued discounting by Birla Opus and JSW. Consolidated margin ~19.0-19.2%, inside management's 18-20% band and in line with brokers (19.0-19.4%). We do not return to FY24's 22.6%: competition has changed the industry's pricing.

segments.name: Subsidiaries & consolidation (international, industrial, decor)
segments._why: Consolidated less standalone revenue grew 10.6% in FY26 (Rs4,815 cr) and 26.9% in Q1FY27 (Rs1,359 cr): international +27% (+20% constant currency; FY26 Rs3,340 cr), Asian Paints PPG +21% (FY26 Rs1,334 cr), Weatherseal +11%, White Teak -7%. FY27 +16% (international ~+15% with Middle East conflict risk and Ethiopia currency, APPPG ~+17%, white cement ramp-up); FY28-29 +11% (international high single digit to low double digit, industrial ~15%).
segments._marginWhy: Consolidated less standalone EBITDA margin: 10.0% (FY20), 5.5% (FY22), 12.7% (FY24), 10.3% (FY25), 10.7% (FY26), 11.6% (Q1FY27). International PBT margin rose to 8.5% (Q4FY26) and 7.9% (Q1FY27) after exiting Indonesia; APPPG PBT margin 6.9-8% (price increases lag); White Teak, Weatherseal and white cement still lose money (FY26 net losses Rs56 cr, Rs23 cr, Rs43 cr). 11% a year: international gains offset by start-up losses.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated (none: the two lines sum to reported EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Standalone plus subsidiaries-and-consolidation equals reported consolidated revenue and EBITDA by construction (history in segments.json).
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash-flow capex Rs2,496 cr (FY24), Rs1,830 cr (FY25), Rs1,487 cr (FY26; standalone Rs1,178 cr). Committed: balance of the ~Rs3,250 cr VAM-VAE project (Dahej, first phase from Aug-2026), a second UAE paint plant (~Rs340 cr), a 4 lakh KL Madhya Pradesh paint plant (~Rs2,000 cr, within three years of environmental clearance), plus ~Rs500-600 cr of maintenance, stores and IT. Rs1,400 cr a year (3.4% of FY27E revenue falling to 3.0%).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs1,229 cr = 8.4% of average gross block (Rs14,707 cr); Q1FY27 Rs304 cr (Rs1,216 cr annualised). The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs1,849 cr at Mar-26) and depreciates capex at once; VAM-VAE capitalisation from FY27 adds depreciation. 8.2% gives Rs1,312 cr in FY27E.

otherTreasury._why: Term deposits with more than 12 months' maturity sit in other financial assets (non-current Rs1,153 cr + current Rs1,285 cr at Mar-26, AR FY26 consolidated note 8), i.e. inside Screener's 'other assets'. They are treasury, not working capital.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to cash, investments and term deposits less borrowings (incl. leases): Rs6,646 cr at Mar-26 (cash Rs1,074 cr + investments Rs7,062 cr + deposits Rs2,439 cr - borrowings Rs3,929 cr). FY26 treasury income (interest Rs181 cr + FVTPL gains Rs287 cr + dividends Rs2 cr = Rs470 cr) was ~5.5% of average gross treasury but ~8.5% of average net cash, because borrowing costs are shown separately as interest. 7.5% on net cash.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: share of profit of the PPG Asian Paints associate (Rs141 cr FY25, Rs166 cr FY26; PPGAP revenue +13.5% in Q1FY27) and other non-operating income ('others' Rs237 cr, royalty, insurance claims ~Rs250 cr in FY26). Rs420 / 450 / 480 cr. FY26 Screener other income (Rs728 cr) was after Rs158 cr of exceptional charges; Q1FY27 Rs279 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs195 cr; Q1FY27 Rs48 cr. Borrowings Rs3,929 cr at Mar-26 incl. Rs1,636 cr leases and Rs805 cr long-term debt taken over with the polymers subsidiary (VAM-VAE).
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: there is no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT Rs2,096 cr, attributable PAT Rs1,539 cr = 26.6% (tax ~25.6% + minorities ~1.0%). FY26: tax Rs1,609 cr on PBT Rs6,003 cr (26.8%, incl. non-deductible exceptional items) and minorities Rs76 cr. Minorities are mainly PPG's 50% of Asian Paints PPG and partners in Nepal, Egypt, Ethiopia, Weatherseal and the UAE white-cement unit.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend policy: 60% of standalone PAT before exceptional items (FY25 and FY26: Rs24.80 and Rs27.50 a share). 60% of consolidated EPS is close to that.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, defensive consumer franchise; below-market sensitivity (Ke 11.3%).
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; paint demand tracks housing, repainting and penetration. The house range is 5-6%; we use 6% for the category leader, as for Pidilite.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~8% to 8% over 15 years: per-capita paint use in India is low, so volume can compound at high single digits for long, but competition caps price and mix.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin ~19.2% in FY29E held near 19%, the middle of management's 18-20% band: the new competitive structure does not allow a return to the 21-22% of FY21/FY24.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~3% of revenue to 3% (maintenance plus regular capacity additions).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Birla Opus and JSW shift from share-chasing to profitability (Nomura's thesis), discounting eases, price increases largely stick as inputs fall, and VAM-VAE delivers its 300-500 bp benefit on a growing share of products; decorative volume 10-11%, standalone margin ~21.5%, consolidated ~20%, the top of the band.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Inflation persists into H2 while competitors keep discounting; Asian Paints cuts prices or raises rebates to defend share, Birla Opus keeps gaining ~30 bp a quarter and JSW Dulux turns aggressive; decorative value growth falls to low single digits in FY28 and consolidated margin slips to ~17.5%, below the 18-20% band (as in FY22 and FY25).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Asian Paints: every broker that discloses a method uses P/E on FY28E EPS (Motilal Oswal, ICICI Securities and Anand Rathi 50x, MNCL 52x, Prabhudas Lilladher ~46.5x; Jul-2026). 43x = the stock's 59.6x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (forwardMedian; no trough years) cut by the ~28% median de-rating of six paint and consumer peers versus their five-year median P/E at 30-Sep-2026 (Berger -27%, Kansai -44%, Indigo -25%, Pidilite -35%, HUL -27%, Astral -29%) = 42.9x. No further growth adjustment: our FY26-29E EPS growth (~14% a year, ~10% after FY27's price boost) is above the 7% of FY21-26, and the competition risk sits in our margin forecast (19%, not 21-22%). 43x is close to the 44x median of the last two years. Bull 48x (its 25th-percentile forward P/E since 2021); bear 38x (~5% below its lowest forward P/E since 2016, 40x).
